ayahs.1: They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: their distribution belongs to Allah and His Messenger—no one owns them by default. So live with taqwa—as though Allah sees you; settle matters among yourselves fairly; and obey Allah and His Messenger if you are truly people of iman, faith that reshapes how you live.
ayahs.2: The true mu'minin are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is remembered, whose iman grows when His ayat are recited to them, and who place their trust in their Rabb—the One who creates, owns, nurtures, and sustains them.
ayahs.3: They are the ones who establish salah, the formal ritual prayer, and give from what We have provided for them.
ayahs.4: Those are the mu'minin in truth. For them are elevated ranks with their Rabb, forgiveness, and a noble provision.
ayahs.5: It is like when your Rabb brought you out of your home for a right cause, and a group among the believers resented it—though the truth had already been made clear.
ayahs.6: They argued with you about the truth after it was plain, as if they were being driven toward death while staring at it.
ayahs.7: Remember when Allah promised you one of two groups—the armed enemy or the unarmed caravan—and you wished for the easier target. But Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the roots of those who reject it.
ayahs.8: So that the truth would stand firm and falsehood be uprooted, even if those steeped in wrongdoing hated it.
ayahs.9: Remember when you cried to your Rabb for help, He answered: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, one rank after another.
ayahs.10: Allah made this only to give you glad news and to settle your hearts. Victory comes only from Allah. Surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
ayahs.11: Remember when He covered you with drowsiness as security from Him, sent rain from the sky to purify you, remove Satan's whispers from you, strengthen your hearts, and make your steps firm.
ayahs.12: Remember when your Rabb revealed to the angels: I am with you. Strengthen the believers. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who reject the truth. So strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of theirs.
ayahs.13: That is because they defied Allah and His Messenger. Whoever defies Allah and His Messenger—know that Allah is severe in punishment.
ayahs.14: That is your taste of worldly punishment—so taste it. Then for those who reject the truth there is the torment of the Fire.
ayahs.15: O you who have iman: when you meet those who reject the truth in battle, do not turn your backs to them.
ayahs.16: Whoever turns back on such a day—unless maneuvering for battle or joining another unit—has drawn Allah's wrath upon himself. His refuge is Jahannam, and what an evil destination.
ayahs.17: You did not kill them when they fell—it was Allah who did. And you did not throw when you threw—it was Allah who threw, to test the believers with a gracious test from Him. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
ayahs.18: That is how Allah frustrates the schemes of those who reject the truth.
ayahs.19: If you Meccans wanted a decisive judgment, it has come to you. If you stop, it is better for you. If you return to hostility, We will return. Your numbers, no matter how great, will not help you. Allah is with the mu'minin.
ayahs.20: O you who have iman: obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear his call.
ayahs.21: Do not be like those who say, "We hear," while they do not truly listen.
ayahs.22: The worst of living beings before Allah are those who refuse to hear and refuse to speak truth—who will not understand.
ayahs.23: Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them listen. Even if He made them listen, they would have turned away in aversion.
ayahs.24: O you who have iman: respond to Allah and His Messenger when he calls you to what gives you life. Know that Allah comes between a person and his heart, and that to Him you will all be gathered.
ayahs.25: Guard against a fitnah, a trial that tests faith, which will not strike only the wrongdoers among you. Know that Allah is severe in punishment.
ayahs.26: Remember when you were few, deemed weak in the land, afraid that people would abduct you—then He gave you shelter, strengthened you with His help, and provided good things, so that you might show shukr, gratitude in word and deed.
ayahs.27: O you who have iman: do not betray Allah and the Messenger, and do not knowingly betray trusts placed in you.
ayahs.28: Know that your wealth and your children are a fitnah—a trial that tests where your heart truly lies—and that with Allah is a tremendous reward.
ayahs.29: O you who have iman: if you live with taqwa, Allah will grant you a clear criterion to distinguish right from wrong, wipe away your sins, and forgive you. Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty.
ayahs.30: Remember when those who reject the truth plotted against you—to imprison you, kill you, or expel you. They plotted, and Allah plotted. Allah is the best of planners.
ayahs.31: When Our ayat are recited to them, they say: "We have heard this before. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but tales of the ancients."
ayahs.32: Remember when they said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain stones on us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."
ayahs.33: But Allah would not punish them while you were among them, nor while they were seeking forgiveness.
ayahs.34: And why should Allah not punish them when they block people from al-Masjid al-Haram, though they are not its rightful guardians? Its guardians are only those who live with taqwa—but most of them do not know.
ayahs.35: Their worship at the Sacred House was only whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment for what you used to reject.
ayahs.36: Those who reject the truth spend their wealth to block the path of Allah. They will keep spending until it becomes a source of regret for them. Then they will be overcome, and toward the Fire they will be driven.
ayahs.37: So Allah may separate the impure from the pure, heap the impure together, and cast them into the Fire. They are the losers.
ayahs.38: Tell those who reject the truth: if they desist, what is past will be forgiven. If they return to hostility, the example of earlier destroyed nations has already gone before them.
ayahs.39: Fight them until there is no more fitnah—no coercion in deen, the way of life aligned with divine guidance—and worship is devoted to Allah alone. If they desist, Allah sees what they do.
ayahs.40: If they turn away, know that Allah is your Protector. What an excellent Protector, and what an excellent Helper.
ayahs.41: Know that whatever you take as spoils, one-fifth belongs to Allah, the Messenger, near relatives, orphans, the poor, and stranded travelers—if you truly believe in Allah and in what We sent down on Our servant on the day the two armies met at Badr. Allah has power over all things.
ayahs.42: Remember when you were on the near side of the valley, they on the far side, and the caravan below you. Even if you had agreed on a meeting time, you would have missed it. But it happened so Allah might carry out a matter already decreed—so that those marked to perish and those marked to live might meet after the truth had been made clear. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
ayahs.43: Remember when Allah showed them to you in your dream as few. Had He shown them as many, you would have faltered and argued about the matter. But Allah saved you from that. He knows what is in the hearts.
ayahs.44: When you met, He made them appear few in your eyes and made you appear few in theirs, so Allah might carry out a matter already decreed. To Allah all matters return.
ayahs.45: O you who have iman: when you meet a force, stand firm and remember Allah much, so you may succeed.
ayahs.46: Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not quarrel with one another, lest you lose heart and your strength depart. Be patient. Surely Allah is with those who practice sabr, steadfast endurance that keeps you upright.
ayahs.47: Do not be like those who left their homes in arrogance, to be seen by people and to turn others from Allah's path. Allah encompasses what they do.
ayahs.48: Remember when Satan made their deeds look fair to them and said: "No one can overcome you today, and I am at your side." But when the two armies came in sight of each other, he turned on his heels and said: "I disown you—I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment."
ayahs.49: Remember when the hypocrites and those with sickness in their hearts said: "These people's iman has deluded them." But whoever puts trust in Allah—Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
ayahs.50: If only you could see when the angels take the souls of those who reject the truth, striking their faces and backs: "Taste the torment of burning."
ayahs.51: That is for what your hands sent ahead. Allah is never unjust to His servants.
ayahs.52: Their end is like that of Pharaoh's people and those before them—they rejected Allah's signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. Allah is All-Powerful, severe in punishment.
ayahs.53: That is because Allah does not change a favor He has bestowed on a people until they change what is within themselves. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
ayahs.54: Their end is like that of Pharaoh's people and those before them—they denied their Rabb's signs, so We destroyed them for their sins and drowned Pharaoh's people. They were all wrongdoers.
ayahs.55: The worst of living beings before Allah are those who persist in rejection and will not believe.
ayahs.56: Those with whom you made a treaty, then break it every time, not living with taqwa.
ayahs.57: If you gain the upper hand over them in war, disperse those behind them by making a severe example, so they may take heed.
ayahs.58: If you fear treachery from a people, announce the dissolution of the treaty to them on equal terms. Allah does not love the treacherous.
ayahs.59: Do not let those who reject the truth think they have escaped. They cannot frustrate Allah.
ayahs.60: Prepare against them whatever military strength and mounted forces you can, to deter Allah's enemies and your enemies—and others you do not know but Allah knows. Whatever you spend in Allah's cause will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.
ayahs.61: If they incline toward peace, incline toward it and put your trust in Allah. He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
ayahs.62: If they intend to deceive you, Allah is sufficient for you. He is the One who supported you with His help and with the believers.
ayahs.63: He united their hearts. If you had spent all that is on earth, you could not have united their hearts—but Allah united them. He is Almighty, All-Wise.
ayahs.64: O Prophet: Allah is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you.
ayahs.65: O Prophet: rouse the believers to fight. If there are twenty steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred. If there are a hundred, they will overcome a thousand of those who reject the truth, because they are a people who do not understand.
ayahs.66: Now Allah has lightened the burden for you, knowing weakness is in you. If there are a hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred. If there are a thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by Allah's permission. Allah is with the steadfast.
ayahs.67: It is not for a prophet to take captives until he has thoroughly subdued the land. You desire the gains of the dunya, this temporary worldly life, while Allah desires the Akhirah, the everlasting life after death. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
ayahs.68: Had it not been for a prior decree from Allah, a severe punishment would have touched you for what you took in ransom.
ayahs.69: So consume what you have taken as lawful and good, and live with taqwa toward Allah. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, the Rahim whose special mercy is reserved for believers in the Akhirah.
ayahs.70: O Prophet, tell the captives in your hands: "If Allah knows good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and forgive you. Allah is All-Forgiving, the Rahim."
ayahs.71: If they intend to betray you, they already betrayed Allah before, and He gave you authority over them. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
ayahs.72: Those who believed, emigrated, and strove with their wealth and lives in Allah's cause, and those who gave shelter and help—they are allies of one another. As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe them no protection until they emigrate. If they seek your help in deen, it is your duty to help them—except against a people with whom you have a treaty. Allah sees what you do.
ayahs.73: Those who reject the truth are allies of one another. Unless you maintain this bond among believers, there will be fitnah and great corruption in the land.
ayahs.74: Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in Allah's cause, and those who gave shelter and help—they are the true mu'minin. For them is forgiveness and a generous provision.
ayahs.75: Those who believed afterward, emigrated, and strove alongside you—they belong to you. But blood relatives are nearer to one another in inheritance, as Allah has decreed. Surely Allah has knowledge of all things.
